_note: `what` must trace to the official rule text and is the only field the fidelity eval checks. `why` is editorial context, human-approved, not claimed as grounded. An entry is served only when reviewed_digest == rule_text_digest. Terminology follows the XRechnung specification: Verkäufer (Seller), Käufer (Buyer).

_sources.UStG: § 14 Abs. 4 UStG, gesetze-im-internet.de/ustg_1980/__14.html — statutory mandatory invoice contents
_sources.BUND: e-rechnung-bund.de/faq/leitweg-id — federal e-invoicing portal, Leitweg-ID FAQ
_sources.L1: the rule text of the named rule in this ruleset (rulesets/2026-08-31)
_sources.MODEL: EN 16931 abstract model, github.com/ConnectingEurope/eInvoicing-EN16931 ubl/schematron/abstract/EN16931-model.sch — BT names
_sources.CL: code list compiled into this ruleset's EN16931-UBL-validation.xsl — the listed example codes are present in it
_sources.SEM: KoSIT semantic model, semantic-model/2026-08-31/xrechnung-semantic-model.xsd (itplr-kosit/xrechnung-visualization) — official German name and description per BT/BG

BR-02.why: An invoice must carry a sequential number that the issuer assigns only once (§ 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 4 UStG).
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [UStG] Nr. 4. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-03.what: The invoice issue date (BT-2) is missing.
BR-03.why: The issue date is a statutory mandatory item (§ 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 3 UStG).
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [UStG] Nr. 3. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-05.what: The invoice currency code (BT-5) is missing.
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: —. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-08.what: The seller's postal address (BG-5) is missing.
BR-08.why: The full name and full address of the supplier are statutory mandatory items (§ 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 1 UStG).
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [UStG] Nr. 1. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-10.what: The buyer's postal address (BG-8) is missing.
BR-10.why: The full name and full address of the recipient are statutory mandatory items (§ 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 1 UStG).
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [UStG] Nr. 1. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-16.what: The invoice contains no invoice line (BG-25).
BR-16.why: Quantity and kind of the goods delivered, or scope and kind of the service, are statutory mandatory items (§ 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 5 UStG). In the standard, the invoice lines (BG-25) carry these details.
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [UStG] Nr. 5; BG-25 is the rule's own term. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-CL-01.what: The document type code is not a permitted code from code list UNTDID 1001.
BR-CL-01.why: The document type is field BT-3 (Invoice type code). An invoice uses code 380, a credit note 381.
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [MODEL] BT-3 via BR-04; [CL] 380, 381. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-CL-04.what: The invoice currency code is not a valid ISO 4217 code.
BR-CL-04.why: A three-letter code from ISO 4217 is expected, for example EUR or CHF.
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [L1] BR-CL-04 says alpha-3; [CL] EUR, CHF. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-CL-14.what: The country code is not a valid ISO 3166-1 code.
BR-CL-14.why: A two-letter code from ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 is expected, for example DE or AT.
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [L1] BR-CO-09 names alpha-2; [CL] DE, AT. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-CL-17.what: The VAT category code is not a permitted code from code list UNCL 5305.
BR-CL-17.why: Permitted codes from UNCL 5305 include S, AE and Z.
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [CL] S, AE, Z — codes only, per the German reviewer decision. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-CO-09.what: The seller VAT identifier (BT-31), the seller tax representative VAT identifier (BT-63) or the buyer VAT identifier (BT-48) does not start with the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country prefix.
BR-CO-09.why: For Germany that means DE123456789, not 123456789. Exception per the rule text: Greece may use the prefix EL.
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [L1] BR-CO-09. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-CO-10.what: The sum of invoice line net amounts (BT-106) does not match the net amounts of the individual lines (BT-131).
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: —. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-CO-13.what: The invoice total amount without VAT (BT-109) does not equal the sum of line net amounts minus document-level allowances plus document-level charges.
BR-CO-13.why: Document-level allowances and charges are fields BT-107 (Sum of allowances on document level) and BT-108 (Sum of charges on document level).
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [MODEL] BT-107, BT-108. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-CO-14.what: The invoice total VAT amount (BT-110) does not equal the sum of the VAT category tax amounts (BT-117).
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: —. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-CO-15.what: The invoice total amount with VAT (BT-112) does not equal the total without VAT plus the VAT amount.
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: —. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-CO-16.what: The amount due for payment (BT-115) does not equal the total with VAT minus the paid amount plus the rounding amount.
BR-CO-16.why: The paid amount is field BT-113 (Paid amount); the rounding amount is BT-114 (Rounding amount).
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [MODEL] BT-113, BT-114. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-DE-1.why: The payment means is given in BT-81 (Payment means type code) — for example credit transfer (codes 30, 58, then with an IBAN in BT-84) or card payment (codes 48, 54, 55).
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [L1] BR-DE-23-a, BR-DE-24-a, BR-DE-19. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-DE-10.what: The city of the delivery address (BT-77) is missing, although the DELIVER TO ADDRESS group (BG-15) is present.
BR-DE-10.why: BG-15 is optional; an invoice with no separate delivery address does not trigger this rule. Once it is given, XRechnung requires it complete: BR-DE-11 additionally requires the post code (BT-78).
review_notes: Mirrors the German entry for BR-DE-10; its review_notes carry the sourcing.

BR-DE-11.what: The post code of the delivery address (BT-78) is missing, although the DELIVER TO ADDRESS group (BG-15) is present.
BR-DE-11.why: BG-15 is optional; an invoice with no separate delivery address does not trigger this rule. Once it is given, XRechnung requires it complete: BR-DE-10 additionally requires the city (BT-77).
review_notes: Mirrors the German entry for BR-DE-11; its review_notes carry the sourcing.

BR-DE-14.what: The VAT category rate (BT-119) is missing.
BR-DE-14.why: EN 16931 allows this field to be omitted when the invoice is not subject to VAT (BR-48). XRechnung removes that exception and requires BT-119 without one. The value feeds the tax calculation: BR-CO-17 requires VAT category tax amount (BT-117) = VAT category taxable amount (BT-116) × BT-119 / 100.
review_notes: Mirrors the German entry for BR-DE-14; its review_notes carry the sourcing.

BR-DE-15.why: The German federal administration uses this field for the Leitweg-ID, by which the federal central invoice intake platform routes the invoice to the responsible office. The contracting authority communicates the Leitweg-ID when placing the order.
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [BUND] — narrowed to the federal level, as in the German entry. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-DE-16.what: The invoice uses one of the VAT category codes S, Z, E, AE, K, G, L or M, but none of the seller's VAT identifier (BT-31), the seller's tax registration identifier (BT-32) or the SELLER TAX REPRESENTATIVE PARTY group (BG-11) is present.
BR-DE-16.why: § 14 (4) of the German VAT Act requires an invoice to carry the supplying trader's tax number or VAT identification number.
review_notes: Mirrors the German entry for BR-DE-16; its review_notes carry the sourcing.

BR-DE-17.what: The invoice type code (BT-3) should be one of the codes 326, 380, 381, 384, 389, 875, 876 or 877 from code list UNTDID 1001.
BR-DE-17.why: 380 (commercial invoice) and 381 (credit note) cover the ordinary cases. Independently of this restriction, BR-CL-01 requires BT-3 to come from UNTDID 1001 at all.
review_notes: Mirrors the German entry for BR-DE-17; its review_notes carry the sourcing.

BR-DE-2.what: The seller contact details (BG-6) are missing.
BR-DE-2.why: The group comprises the contact point (BT-41), its telephone number (BT-42) and its email address (BT-43); XRechnung requires each of these fields individually (BR-DE-5, BR-DE-6, BR-DE-7).
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [L1] BR-DE-5/6/7. Not yet reviewed in English.
Reviewer decision 2026-09-09: 'The seller contact is missing' read as though a person were absent; 'contact details' matches the German Kontaktdaten and the group's content.

BR-DE-23-a.what: The payment means (BT-81) is a credit transfer (code 30 or 58), but the CREDIT TRANSFER group (BG-17) is missing.
BR-DE-23-a.why: BT-81 states how the invoice is to be paid. BG-17 carries the bank account the transfer is to be made to. BR-DE-23-b conversely requires the other two account groups to be absent.
review_notes: Mirrors the German entry for BR-DE-23-a; its review_notes carry the sourcing.

BR-DE-23-b.what: The payment means (BT-81) is a credit transfer (code 30 or 58), but the invoice contains the PAYMENT CARD INFORMATION group (BG-18) or the DIRECT DEBIT group (BG-19), neither of which may then be present.
BR-DE-23-b.why: The other half of BR-DE-23-a: for a credit transfer the account details belong in BG-17, and the card and direct debit groups have no place in the same invoice.
review_notes: Mirrors the German entry for BR-DE-23-b; its review_notes carry the sourcing.

BR-DE-24-a.what: The payment means (BT-81) is a card payment (code 48, 54 or 55), but the PAYMENT CARD INFORMATION group (BG-18) is missing.
BR-DE-24-a.why: BG-18 carries the details of the card used. BR-DE-24-b conversely requires the other two account groups to be absent.
review_notes: Mirrors the German entry for BR-DE-24-a; its review_notes carry the sourcing.

BR-DE-24-b.what: The payment means (BT-81) is a card payment (code 48, 54 or 55), but the invoice contains the CREDIT TRANSFER group (BG-17) or the DIRECT DEBIT group (BG-19), neither of which may then be present.
BR-DE-24-b.why: The other half of BR-DE-24-a: for a card payment the details belong in BG-18, and the credit transfer and direct debit groups have no place in the same invoice.
review_notes: Mirrors the German entry for BR-DE-24-b; its review_notes carry the sourcing.

BR-DE-25-a.what: The payment means (BT-81) is a direct debit (code 59), but the DIRECT DEBIT group (BG-19) is missing.
BR-DE-25-a.why: BG-19 carries the details of the intended direct debit and is given when a mandate has been granted. BR-DE-30 and BR-DE-31 additionally require the bank assigned creditor identifier (BT-90) and the debited account identifier (BT-91) within it.
review_notes: Mirrors the German entry for BR-DE-25-a; its review_notes carry the sourcing.

BR-DE-25-b.what: The payment means (BT-81) is a direct debit (code 59), but the invoice contains the CREDIT TRANSFER group (BG-17) or the PAYMENT CARD INFORMATION group (BG-18), neither of which may then be present.
BR-DE-25-b.why: The other half of BR-DE-25-a: for a direct debit the details belong in BG-19, and the credit transfer and card groups have no place in the same invoice.
review_notes: Mirrors the German entry for BR-DE-25-b; its review_notes carry the sourcing.

BR-DE-3.why: The full address is a statutory mandatory item (§ 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 1 UStG); XRechnung makes city (BT-37) and post code (BT-38) separate mandatory fields (BR-DE-3, BR-DE-4).
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [UStG] Nr. 1; [L1] BR-DE-3/4. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-DE-30.what: The DIRECT DEBIT group (BG-19) is present, but the bank assigned creditor identifier (BT-90) is missing.
BR-DE-30.why: BT-90 is the creditor identifier with which the seller or payee takes part in the SEPA direct debit scheme. BR-DE-31 additionally requires the debited account identifier (BT-91) in the same group.
review_notes: Mirrors the German entry for BR-DE-30; its review_notes carry the sourcing.

BR-DE-31.what: The DIRECT DEBIT group (BG-19) is present, but the debited account identifier (BT-91) is missing.
BR-DE-31.why: BT-91 is, within SEPA, the IBAN of the account the direct debit is to be taken from. BR-DE-30 additionally requires the bank assigned creditor identifier (BT-90) in the same group.
review_notes: Mirrors the German entry for BR-DE-31; its review_notes carry the sourcing.

BR-DE-4.what: The seller post code (BT-38) is missing.
BR-DE-4.why: The full address is a statutory mandatory item (§ 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 1 UStG); XRechnung makes city (BT-37) and post code (BT-38) separate mandatory fields (BR-DE-3, BR-DE-4).
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [UStG] Nr. 1; [L1] BR-DE-3/4. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-DE-5.what: The seller's contact point (BT-41) is missing.
BR-DE-5.why: BR-DE-2 requires the SELLER CONTACT group (BG-6); BR-DE-5, BR-DE-6 and BR-DE-7 require its three fields individually: the contact point (BT-41), the telephone number (BT-42) and the email address (BT-43).
review_notes: Mirrors the German entry for BR-DE-5; its review_notes carry the sourcing.

BR-DE-6.what: The seller contact telephone number (BT-42) is missing.
BR-DE-6.why: Contact point (BT-41), telephone number (BT-42) and email address (BT-43) together form the SELLER CONTACT group (BG-6), which XRechnung requires (BR-DE-2, BR-DE-5 to BR-DE-7).
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [L1] BR-DE-2, BR-DE-5/6/7. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-DE-7.what: The seller contact email address (BT-43) is missing.
BR-DE-7.why: Contact point (BT-41), telephone number (BT-42) and email address (BT-43) together form the SELLER CONTACT group (BG-6), which XRechnung requires (BR-DE-2, BR-DE-5 to BR-DE-7).
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [L1] BR-DE-2, BR-DE-5/6/7. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-DE-8.why: The full address of the recipient is a statutory mandatory item (§ 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 1 UStG); XRechnung makes city (BT-52) and post code (BT-53) separate mandatory fields (BR-DE-8, BR-DE-9).
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [UStG] Nr. 1; [L1] BR-DE-8/9. Not yet reviewed in English.

BR-DE-9.what: The buyer post code (BT-53) is missing.
BR-DE-9.why: The full address of the recipient is a statutory mandatory item (§ 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 1 UStG); XRechnung makes city (BT-52) and post code (BT-53) separate mandatory fields (BR-DE-8, BR-DE-9).
review_notes: Drafted 2026-09-08 from the German entry reviewed by Harshal on 2026-09-08. Same sources: [UStG] Nr. 1; [L1] BR-DE-8/9. Not yet reviewed in English.
